transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

My sleep has been completely off for weeks—either I’m up most of the night with my mind going or I crash and still wake up feeling completely worn out. My primary care doctor urgently referred me here because of how much this and my mood changes have been affecting my life, but right now I just feel so exhausted.
Can you tell me more about these mood changes you've been experiencing, such as feeling sad, anxious, or irritable, and how they relate to your sleep disturbances?

On my 'up' days when I'm irritable and snapping at my family, I only get about three or four hours of sleep but still wake up feeling completely wired and full of energy. But when that heavy gray cloud of sadness and guilt settles over me, I either lie awake for hours with my mind racing or crash completely and still wake up feeling totally exhausted.
Can you estimate how many days in a typical week you experience these 'up' days with excessive energy and irritability versus the days with overwhelming sadness and guilt?

It's really hard to put an exact number of days on it because the swings feel so unpredictable and just run together. But both of these states have been happening on and off for about three months now, ever since things got so stressful at home.

Can you help me understand if there are distinct periods where you're mostly experiencing the 'up' moods with energy, followed by periods of mostly 'down' moods with sadness, or if these moods are interspersed throughout your days without clear episodes?

They definitely feel like distinct stretches rather than jumping back and forth from hour to hour. I'll have these wired, overdrive spells where my energy is through the roof—which is actually the only time I hear those voices calling my name—and then I'll crash into a heavy, low period where I just feel completely useless and guilty. This pattern of going between these distinct phases has been going on for about three months now.
Can you describe the typical duration of these 'up' periods with excessive energy and the 'down' periods with sadness, and do you experience any periods of normal mood in between these episodes?

These intense ups and downs have been going on for about three months now, ever since my daughter moved back in and my mom's health declined. During these months, it has felt like a constant roller coaster where I'm either wound up or completely crashed. I really haven't had any periods of 'normal' or stable mood in between.
Can you estimate the shortest and longest duration of these 'up' or 'down' periods, and do you ever experience a shift from one extreme to the other within a single day?

I'm not quite sure about the exact shortest or longest duration of these periods, or if I completely switch from one extreme to the other in a single day. The overall cycle of these ups and downs has been going on for about three months now. While my mood can swing quickly from feeling on top of the world to snapping at someone, I just don't know the exact timing of it all.

Can you clarify if you've experienced at least one period of abnormally elevated or irritable mood lasting at least one week, or if these 'up' periods are significantly shorter, and how they contrast with your 'down' periods?

Yes, those 'up' periods definitely last for days or even weeks at a time, where I feel on top of the world and full of energy but also highly irritable and quick to snap at everyone. In contrast, during the 'down' periods, a heavy gray cloud settles over me and leaves me feeling completely exhausted, useless, and guilty. This whole pattern has been going on for about three months now.

Can you confirm if you've had at least one episode of elevated or irritable mood that lasted for at least one week, and another episode of depressed mood that lasted for at least two weeks, within these three months?

Yes, I have definitely experienced both of those. The wired, high-energy periods where I'm irritable and snapping at everyone last for at least a week at a time. The heavy, depressed crashes last even longer—sometimes for weeks on end—over these past three months.
